owner: opt, lm, train -- the numeric levers
summary:
SURFACE AND DENOMINATOR. Enumerated from each package's levers.py, a Lever whose default is an int or a float and not a bool: OPT 11 (lr, weight_decay, grad_clip, lr_warmup, lr_wavelength, lr_min_frac, lr_restart_damp, lr_decay, lr_shift_warm, batch_windows, accum), LM 8 (width, layers, heads, ctx, dropout, vocab_slots, anchor_w, anchor_uses), RUN/train 2 (epochs, seed). TWENTY-ONE numeric levers, not the estimated 21-ish-as-about-21 -- 21 exactly. Four values each (nan, inf, -inf, 0) = 84 CELLS, every one driven in a FRESH SUBPROCESS through a real spine.assemble.build(environ=...) and then through the package's live entry points: OPT.build -> OPT.lr_at over an 8-point step grid -> 6 x (scaled_backward, maybe_step with a (value, seed_count) Reading) -> OPT.counters; LM.resolve -> LM.build_model -> LM.encode -> LM.decode (and LM.anchor_term / LM.counters, which are P4 stubs); RUN.process_setup -> RUN.mode -> RUN.streams -> RUN.startup_refusals both ways on disk_stream. Every cell's output was captured; nothing here is inferred from reading.

COUNTS PER OUTCOME, ALL 84 CELLS:
  REFUSED_BY_NAME      36
  REFUSED_BADLY        26
  ACCEPTED_HARMFUL      5
  ACCEPTED_LEGITIMATE  11
  ACCEPTED_INERT        0
  UNREACHABLE_TODAY     6
  CRASHED               0

THE FIVE HARMFUL CELLS, AND FOUR OF THEM ARE ONE DEFECT. OPT_LR=inf and OPT_WEIGHT_DECAY=inf each put NaN into EVERY parameter of the base group within two optimizer steps, with the whole ledger reporting a healthy run -- critical, and the same shape as FAB_BALANCE=nan one lever over. OPT_GRAD_CLIP=nan turns clipping silently off at a measured gradient norm of 8.0e6 AND makes src/opt/api.py::counters print the literal string 'off (0.0)' plus the sentence "OPT_GRAD_CLIP=0.0 is OFF, which is the setting every recorded number in this project was measured under" -- a report asserting a value the operator did not type. OPT_LR_RESTART_DAMP=nan kills this package's ONLY closed loop (the goal-B restart damping) while the gate prints the armed-but-did-not-fire verdict over 3 real losing restarts and 1000 readings. OPT_GRAD_CLIP=inf is the low one: a cap that cannot bite, reported as armed.

THE COMMON ROOT, WHICH IS WHAT THE RULING PHASE NEEDS. Every guard that failed is a ONE-SIDED ORDER COMPARISON -- `lr <= 0.0`, `weight_decay < 0.0`, `grad_clip < 0.0`, `damp > 1.0`, `damp < 0.0`, `anchor_uses <= 0`, `clip > 0.0`, `lr_restart_damp < 1.0` -- and NaN is ordered against nothing, so it passes all of them; +inf additionally passes every lower bound. Every guard that HELD against NaN has the inverted-chain form: `if not 0.0 <= min_frac < 1.0`, `if not 0.0 <= decay <= 1.0`, `if not 0.0 <= dropout < 1.0`. Three levers are safe today by grammar, not by intent. That distinction is the sweep's main structural result: a per-package repair means auditing every one-sided comparison in three files; a central rule in src/spine/lever.py::Lever.coerce covers all of them at the one place a string becomes a float.

THE SECOND ROOT, AND IT IS ALREADY CENTRAL. 24 of the 26 REFUSED_BADLY cells are ONE line: src/spine/lever.py::Lever.coerce runs `v = int(float(raw))` under `except (TypeError, ValueError)`, and int(float('inf')) raises OverflowError, which is an ArithmeticError and escapes uncaught. Every int-defaulted lever in the tree -- all 12 on this surface, and by construction every int lever in the other ten packages -- answers +inf and -inf with a bare `OverflowError: cannot convert float infinity to integer` naming no lever, no environment variable and not even the sign. One line above it, 'nan' takes the ValueError branch and produces the tree's own idiom. Adding OverflowError to that except tuple is a one-token fix that converts 24 of these cells to REFUSED_BY_NAME with no policy decision at all, and it is independent of whatever the ruling phase decides about non-finite floats.

WHAT THE REFUSALS GOT RIGHT, since the denominator matters both ways. 36 of 84 cells refused by name with the lever, the value and the reason, at the earliest layer that could see them: all eleven of src/opt/api.py::build's startup refusals fire correctly on -inf, six of LM.resolve's geometry refusals fire on 0, and the 12 'nan' cells on int levers are refused cleanly by src/spine/lever.py::Lever.coerce. -inf is caught far more often than nan or +inf for exactly the reason the brief names: it is caught INCIDENTALLY, because it happens to be negative, by guards written about sign.

REACHABILITY, STATED PRECISELY. src/spine/compose.py::compose halts at src/capacity/api.py::startup_refusals -- row 29 of ASSEMBLY_ORDER's 39 -- verified by running it (NotImplementedError: "CAP.startup_refusals: P4 (capacity) fills this in."). That is BEFORE the `optimizer` stage where src/spine/compose.py calls opt_api.build, so no OPT finding here is reachable through the root today. That is NOT the same as a latent hole: OPT.build, OPT.lr_at and OPT.maybe_step are fully implemented and were driven directly, and they arm the instant the CAP stub lands. The genuinely latent cases are the six UNREACHABLE_TODAY cells, where the CONSUMER itself is the stub: LM_ANCHOR_W (all four values -- src/lm/api.py::resolve does not read it at all, and its only readers src/lm/api.py::anchor_term and src/lm/api.py::counters both raise NotImplementedError) and LM_ANCHOR_USES at nan and inf (resolve's `<= 0` guard admits them; the horizon is read only by the anchor_term stub). RUN's findings are reachable through the root today -- process_setup and startup_refusals are rows 1 and 6.

NO CELL CRASHED and no cell was ACCEPTED_INERT: every accepted value either damaged something, meant something declared, or could not reach its consumer.

One optimizer step drives every parameter in the base group to -inf and the second to NaN. Nothing anywhere says a word: OPT.build returns a normal-looking Horizon(run_steps=1000, warmup=100, wavelength=1000, n_cycles=1), src/opt/api.py::counters returns a full ledger, and the only trace is opt.grad_norm.p50=inf / p99=nan buried among 40 counters. This is the FAB_BALANCE=nan shape one lever over: a magnitude guard written as `<= 0` that a non-finite value is not ordered against. findings.detail: Two guards miss it and a third prints a value the operator never typed. src/opt/api.py::build refuses only `grad_clip < 0.0` (False for NaN). src/opt/api.py::maybe_step then gates the clip on `if clip > 0.0:` (also False for NaN), so gradient clipping is SILENTLY OFF at any gradient magnitude -- measured with grad norms of 8.0e6 and zero clip events. The damage is the report, and it is the exact FAB_BALANCE=nan shape: src/opt/api.py::counters builds Gate('opt.build.grad_clip', clip > 0.0, clip if clip > 0.0 else 'off (0.0)', ...), so the gate's VALUE renders as the literal string 'off (0.0)' and its reason is the hard-coded sentence "OPT_GRAD_CLIP=0.0 is OFF, which is the setting every recorded number in this project was measured under (Q-OPT-3)". An operator who typed nan reads a report asserting they typed 0.0 and that the run matches every historical baseline. The very next gate, opt.clip.applied, interpolates the real value and prints 'OPT_GRAD_CLIP=nan is OFF' -- so one line of the same ledger contradicts the other.

findings.detail: Accepted (`inf < 0.0` is False), and the clip branch in src/opt/api.py::maybe_step DOES run -- but `norm > clip` is False for every finite norm, so the cap is structurally incapable of biting. src/opt/api.py::counters then reports it in the ARMED-BUT-0 state: Gate('opt.build.grad_clip') fires with value=inf and reachable=True, and Gate('opt.clip.applied') prints reachable=True with the reason "armed and NOTHING exceeded the norm -- a different statement from grad_clip == 0" -- on a run whose measured gradient norms were 8.0e6. That sentence is the tree's word for 'the mechanism ran and its condition was not met', and here the condition CANNOT be met. The tree's own DID IT FIRE rule has three states and requires UNREACHABLE to be named with the lever and value; this is the second state printed for the third. Low severity because the run is undamaged: an operator wanting no clipping already has the declared sentinel 0.0.

findings.detail: The two magnitude refusals in src/opt/api.py::build are `damp > 1.0` and `damp < 0.0`, and NaN is ordered against neither, so it is admitted while +inf and -inf are both refused by name from the same pair of lines. Downstream, clause 4 of src/opt/api.py::maybe_step is `if not paid and float(opt.lr_restart_damp) < 1.0:` -- also False for NaN -- so the ONE closed loop this package owns, the goal-B mechanism that shrinks a restart that failed to beat its inherited held-out, is silently dead. It takes none of the three declared exits: opt.restart.damped, opt.restart.damp_refused_n1 and opt.restart.no_reading all stay 0. Driven 1000 steps over a 4-cycle horizon with a LOSING Reading (value, seed_count) on every step: at the shipped damp=0.5 the mechanism fires twice and restart_amp lands at 0.25; at damp=nan, with the identical 3 wraps, 3 detected restarts and 1000 readings, it fires ZERO times and restart_amp stays 1.0 -- and src/opt/api.py::counters prints Gate 'opt.lr.restart_damp' with reachable=True, fired=False, i.e. the ARMED-BUT-DID-NOT-FIRE verdict, whose threshold field reads 'damp=nan, refused_n1=0, no_reading=0, readings=1000'. A reader concludes no cycle ever lost. Three did.

findings.detail: src/lm/api.py::resolve DOES guard this lever -- `if float(lm.anchor_uses) <= 0:` -- and that guard catches 0 and -inf by name. It is an order comparison, so NaN slips through it exactly as `lr <= 0.0` lets NaN through in OPT; +inf slips through because it is genuinely above zero. At NaN the release test `seen < anchor_uses` would be False for every token -- every minted token released IMMEDIATELY, which is the exact opposite of the state the existing refusal calls 'hold every minted token at its composite forever'. At +inf it is that state literally, and the refusal that exists to prevent it does not fire. Latent, not absent: it arms when P4 (lm) fills anchor_term in.

legitimate_specials:
OPT_WEIGHT_DECAY=0 -- weight decay OFF; the shipped default. Declared: src/opt/levers.py::OPTLevers weight_decay ("AdamW decoupled weight decay, applied to the base optimizer and the encoder optimizer alike") with default 0.0, and src/opt/api.py::build refuses only `weight_decay < 0.0`.
OPT_GRAD_CLIP=0 -- clipping OFF, stated in the declaration itself. Declared: src/opt/levers.py::OPTLevers grad_clip ("0.0 is OFF, which is what every recorded number in this project was measured under"), and src/opt/api.py::counters gives it a dedicated UNREACHABLE gate arm: "OPT_GRAD_CLIP=0.0 is OFF, so no step can clip. This is not 'armed and did not fire'."
OPT_LR_WARMUP=0 -- NO warmup: the cosine spans the run from step 0. Declared: src/opt/api.py::_cycle_index ("at a horizon whose warmup resolved to 0 -- which build() permits, since only a NEGATIVE lr_warmup is refused ... at warmup 0 there is no warmup, so the cosine spans the run from step 0"), and src/opt/api.py::build refuses only `lr_warmup < 0`. VERIFIED: horizon came back Horizon(run_steps=Steps(1000), warmup=Steps(0), ...) and lr_at(1) = 0.00199999 (peak) instead of the 2e-05 first rung of the default ramp.
OPT_LR_WAVELENGTH=0 -- THE SENTINEL: one wavelength spans the whole run. Declared verbatim in src/opt/levers.py::OPTLevers lr_wavelength ("0 means one wavelength spans the whole run") and resolved in exactly one visible place in src/opt/api.py::build (`wavelength = run_steps if from_sentinel else U.Steps(...)`), counted as opt.build.wavelength_from_sentinel. VERIFIED: identical rates to the default and opt.build.wavelength_from_sentinel = 1.
OPT_LR_MIN_FRAC=0 -- the schedule HAS no floor and anneals to zero; a legal setting the report warns about rather than refuses. Declared: src/opt/api.py::build refuses only outside [0.0, 1.0), and src/opt/api.py::counters carries a dedicated arm, "OPT_LR_MIN_FRAC=0.0: the clamp is max(0.0, cyc) over a cosine that is already non-negative, so no step can be raised by it and the schedule HAS no floor -- which is the setting lr_min_frac's goal-B argument exists to warn about." VERIFIED: lr_at(1000) = 0.0 against 0.0001 at the default.
OPT_LR_RESTART_DAMP=0 -- the restart swing collapses to the floor on the first losing cycle and stays there. Declared by the refusal boundary in src/opt/api.py::build (`damp < 0.0` refused, 0.0 admitted) and by the arithmetic in src/opt/api.py::maybe_step clause 4 (`st.restart_amp *= float(opt.lr_restart_damp)`). VERIFIED at 4 cycles: 3 wraps, 2 detected (one fewer than at damp=0.5, because the collapsed amplitude blinds the detector -- the inversion src/opt/api.py::maybe_step's own docstring documents), 1 damped, restart_amp = 0.0.
OPT_LR_DECAY=0 -- envelope OFF; restarts return to full peak. Declared verbatim in the refusal text in src/opt/api.py::build ("0.0 restores the pre-2026-08-26 behaviour (restarts return to full peak) and 1.0 is the full envelope"). VERIFIED: opt.lr.envelope_applied stayed 0 over 1000 driven steps.
OPT_LR_SHIFT_WARM=0 -- the post-shift re-warm is OFF, and the tree insists this is a DIFFERENT statement from "nobody is supplying shift_at". Declared: src/opt/levers.py::OPTLevers lr_shift_warm block ("`opt.shift.notifications` at 0 means NOBODY IS SUPPLYING shift_at, which is a different statement from lr_shift_warm == 0, and the report must make both"), and src/opt/api.py::_schedule gates the re-warm on `bool(shift_warm)`.
OPT_BATCH_WINDOWS=1 / OPT_ACCUM=1 are the shipped defaults; 0 is refused for both and is NOT a sentinel. Recorded here only so the ruling phase does not mistake them for one.
LM_LAYERS=0 -- THE SENTINEL: take this arm's default depth (4 on transformer, 1 on gru). Declared in src/lm/api.py::resolve ("the lever's 0 sentinel replaced by 4 on the transformer arm and 1 on the gru arm ... 0 layers is not a small model, it is a broken constructor") and recorded on the geometry as layers_from_sentinel plus counter lm.resolve.layers_from_sentinel. VERIFIED: LMGeometry(... layers=1 ... layers_from_sentinel=True) and a working forward pass.
LM_DROPOUT=0 -- dropout OFF; the shipped default. Declared: src/lm/api.py::resolve refuses only outside [0.0, 1.0), and src/train/api.py::process_setup's docstring treats LM_DROPOUT=0.0 as the determinism-clean case ("the SAME pair of processes at LM_DROPOUT=0.0 agreed exactly").
RUN_SEED=0 -- the shipped root seed, a real value and not "unset". Declared: src/train/levers.py::RUNLevers seed, default 0, and src/spine/rng.py::derive_seed is blake2b of (seed, name) so 0 is an ordinary seed. VERIFIED: Process.torch_seed = 3734753547471956429 and named streams minted (memory seed=5876198497521010688, domains seed=905312284192048243).
NOT A SENTINEL, stated so the ruling phase does not add one: RUN_EPOCHS=0 is REFUSED by name in src/train/api.py::startup_refusals, deliberately rather than clamped; OPT_LR=0 is refused by src/opt/api.py::build; LM_WIDTH/LM_HEADS/LM_CTX/LM_VOCAB_SLOTS=0 and LM_ANCHOR_USES=0 are all refused by name in src/lm/api.py::resolve.
